claims.text: A Zr-getter atmosphere generated in situ from ZrH2 will enable complete dehydrogenation of the precursor hydrides.
The Zr getter will maintain oxygen partial pressure below 10^-15 atm.
Maintaining this oxygen partial pressure will suppress alpha-HCP nucleation.
Rapid quenching from 1250°C will retain a metastable single-phase beta-BCC structure.
Localized hydride decomposition will induce transient liquid-phase sintering.
Transient liquid-phase sintering will refine the grain size to the sub-micron scale.
The starting equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr powder blend has an oxygen content of approximately 500-1000 ppm.
A slow ramp to 800°C will drive sequential decomposition of TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2.
The reaction Zr + O2 to ZrO2 will suppress oxygen diffusion into the alloy lattice.
Preventing oxygen uptake will prevent thermodynamic stabilization of the alpha-HCP phase.
Hydrogen released by sequential hydride decomposition will create a reducing environment.
The alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC transformation is diffusion controlled and can be bypassed by rapid quenching.
The proposed treatment will produce a nearly fully dense alloy with greater than 98% density.
The quenched alloy will have a grain size of 0.5-2.0 µm.
The quenched alloy will contain no alpha-HCP or alpha-Ti precipitates.
Sintering this alloy in pure argon without a getter typically produces either alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC or alpha-HCP plus beta-BCC microstructures.
Pure-argon sintering without a getter typically causes significant oxygen-induced embrittlement.
Pure-argon sintering without a getter typically produces grain sizes greater than 5 µm because of slower kinetics.
Getter exhaustion will cause the proposed oxygen-control mechanism to fail.
An excessively slow heating rate will allow oxygen diffusion to outpace oxygen scavenging.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes the grain size as sub-micron, whereas the predicted range extends to 2.0 µm and is therefore not wholly sub-micron.

The operating and boundary criterion requires pO2 below 10^-15 atm, but the falsification rule only rejects oxygen pressures above 10^-14 atm, leaving an order-of-magnitude interval that violates the stated requirement without falsifying the hypothesis.

Transient liquid formation is asserted as an operative mediator, while the uncertainty field states that decomposition overlap only could produce such a liquid, making the mediator less established than the main hypothesis implies.
